classification.difficultyReason: Recognise each quadrilateral as an unordered selection of four vertices.

content.prompt: How many quadrilaterals can be formed by joining any 4 vertices of a regular octagon?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, below the prompt in the right column
spec.description: Regular octagon with an example quadrilateral joining the top, right, lower-right and left vertices. The source cyan fill is omitted under the unshaded house convention; the quadrilateral remains visible through its outline.
spec.mathematics: Eight vertices in cyclic order; the example quadrilateral uses vertices 1, 3, 4 and 7 when counting clockwise from the top.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied example quadrilateral is permanently visible; no numerical answer is shown.

answer.worked:
Each selection of four vertices determines one quadrilateral, and the order of selection is irrelevant.
$$\begin{align*}
\binom{8}{4} &= \frac{8!}{4!4!}\\
\binom{8}{4} &= \frac{8\times7\times6\times5}{4\times3\times2\times1}\\
\binom{8}{4} &= 70.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $70$ quadrilaterals can be formed.
